sourcedFrom: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 (2026)
cleanIntro: The .308 SCAR: same modular takedown as the 16S — takedown pin, trigger module, buttstock module, then the moving parts assembly out of the back — on a heavier receiver working a bigger cartridge. This is FN's second-generation book, which strips two charging handles and a charging sled, so the first thing to settle is which generation of 17S you own.

steps.title: Second generation, NRCH, or original — decide before you start
steps.action: Look at the charging handle. This manual describes the second generation FN SCAR 17S and its strip pulls two charging handles and a charging sled out of the receiver. A single handle that travels with the bolt as the rifle fires means an earlier 17S, and FN publishes a separate book for those.
steps.prose: FN's giveaway is the notice in the firing section referring to current and previous SCAR rifles fitted with non-reciprocating charging handles — a sentence that only appears in a book written after both the 2016 original and the 2021 NRCH edition. On a .308 this is worth an extra ten seconds: the moving parts in a 17S are heavier and under more spring load, and hunting for a part that does not exist while a receiver is half apart is how things get forced.
steps.aside: The book's own scope line from the page 2 block: Second generation FN SCAR® 16S, 17S and 20S Autoloading Rifles.
steps.quote: NOTICE! THE CHARGING HANDLES ON CURRENT AND PREVIOUS FN SCAR RIFLES EQUIPPED WITH NONRECIPROCATING CHARGING HANDLE (NRCH) WILL NOT MOVE AS THE RIFLE CYCLES.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §14.1 Firing procedures, notice, p.26

steps.title: Confirm the chambering, and know your magazine pattern
steps.action: Read the caliber marking on the barrel near the muzzle and confirm it matches what you are loading. Then note the magazines: a 17S takes 20 rounds as standard, and it shares its magazine pattern with the 20S — not with the 16S.
steps.prose: This is the one place where the three rifles in this manual are genuinely easy to confuse, because the receivers look alike and the magazine wells do not accept each other's magazines. A 16S magazine holds 30 and belongs to a different pattern; a 20S magazine holds 10 and will fit a 17S. So a magazine that goes in but only holds ten is not faulty, it is a 20S magazine, and one that will not go in at all is probably a 5.56 magazine from a 16S.
steps.aside: FN's capacities: FN SCAR 16S rifles have a standard magazine capacity of 30 rounds. FN SCAR 17S rifles have a standard magazine capacity of 20 rounds.
steps.quote: FN SCAR 17S and 20S rifles share the same magazine pattern.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §12 Magazine capacity, p.22
steps.warn: The FN SCAR 16S, 17S and 20S magazines are unique for the rifles and should not be used in other rifles. No other magazine type should be used in your rifles.

steps.title: Selector on safe, magazine out
steps.action: Put the safety selector in the on-safe position with the muzzle pointed somewhere safe, then press the ambidextrous magazine release just forward of the trigger guard and take the magazine out with your free hand.
steps.prose: A loaded 20-round .308 magazine is heavy and the release works from both sides, so catch it rather than letting it fall — a dropped SCAR magazine lands on its feed lips. Take it fully clear before touching the charging handle: with a magazine still seated, cycling the action loads the rifle rather than clearing it. Selector stays on safe from here to the end of the strip.
steps.quote: Press the ambidextrous magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §15.1 Unloading the rifle, step 2, p.29

steps.title: Bolt locked open by hand, chamber inspected
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to draw the bolt fully rearward, press the ambidextrous bolt lock to hold it open, then look into the chamber and confirm no live cartridge is present.
steps.prose: FN spells out that the bolt will not lock back on its own when the magazine has been removed or when a loaded magazine is in place — you press the lock yourself. That is the failure this step exists to catch: a bolt that ran forward behind you looks and feels identical to a rifle you already cleared. A .308 case in the chamber is large and obvious once you actually put your eye to the ejection port.
steps.quote: pulling rearward on the charging handle to draw the bolt to its rearmost, open position and pressing the ambidextrous bolt lock as explained in Section 10.2. Please note that the bolt will not automatically lock in the rearward position when the magazine is removed or when a loaded magazine is present. As a good safety practice, hold the bolt open and visually inspect the chamber to be absolutely certain a live cartridge is not present (Figure 18).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §15.1 Unloading the rifle, step 3, p.29

steps.title: Close the bolt on a confirmed empty chamber
steps.action: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty, close the bolt and make certain the safety selector is still on safe before you start taking anything off.
steps.prose: The takedown pin will not push cleanly with the bolt locked to the rear, so the strip begins from a closed bolt — which is exactly why the chamber gets confirmed first. Closing the bolt on an empty chamber is a deliberate act, not something to do absent-mindedly while reaching for a pin punch. Everything from here is finger pressure only.
steps.quote: With the magazine removed and the chamber empty, close the bolt. Make certain the safety selector is in the “on safe” position and properly store your rifle.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §15.1 Unloading the rifle, step 4, p.30

steps.title: Gas regulator to the 3 o'clock disassembly setting
steps.action: Viewed from the muzzle, cycle the gas regulator two or three times so it is moving freely, then set it to 3 o'clock — the position FN designates for disassembly, cleaning and reassembly.
steps.prose: The 17S has the same three-position regulator as the rest of the family: 2 o'clock standard, 10 o'clock suppressed, 3 o'clock for taking it apart. Cycling it first is FN's own recommendation and doubles as a carbon check — a regulator that has gone stiff on a .308 is a warning, because most of the carbon is supposed to be blowing out through the vent hole in the front of it. Set it before anything else moves, since you will need it there again to get the piston out later.
steps.quote: 3 o’clock setting - Disassembly, cleaning, and reassembly (Figure 17).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §14.2 Adjusting the gas regulator, p.28

steps.title: Takedown pin pushed from the left, pulled to the right
steps.action: Push the takedown pin in from the left side and pull it out to the right until it stops. It is captive and will not come all the way out.
steps.prose: Finger pressure and nothing else — FN's own instruction for this whole procedure is that it is designed to be done with finger pressure only and that if you cannot, you stop and contact the FN Service Center. The pin stopping partway is correct behaviour, not a jam. Lay the rifle flat first so a sling or a mounted bipod is not holding the modules in tension while the pin moves.
steps.caution: IMPORTANT: THE TAKEDOWN PIN IS CAPTIVE AND CANNOT BE REMOVED COMPLETELY FROM THE TRIGGER MODULE.
steps.quote: Push in on the takedown pin from the left side (Figure 31) and pull it out to the right until it stops (Figure 32).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.1 Removal of the trigger module, step 2, p.36

steps.title: Trigger module forward off the backplate, then down
steps.action: Push the trigger module forward to release it from the backplate, then pull it down and out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Forward, then down. The module engages the backplate at the rear, so pulling straight down against that engagement only flexes it. It should come away as one sealed unit and it stays that way — FN's instruction is not to alter or disassemble any part of the trigger module, and the trigger has been set at the factory to a pull that is not meant to be changed.
steps.aside: FN's preceding instruction: Push the trigger module forward, releasing it from the from the backplate (Figure 33).
steps.quote: Pull down to remove the trigger module from the receiver (Figure 34).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.1 Removal of the trigger module, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Carbine buttstock module down and off
steps.action: With the trigger module out, push the buttstock module downward and off the receiver assembly backplate.
steps.prose: The 17S wears the same side-folding carbine buttstock as the 16S — FN gives them a shared section heading and gives the 20S a different SSR stock in a section of its own. It slides down off the backplate rather than pulling rearward, and it comes off just as easily folded or unfolded, provided it is not locked against the shell deflector. If your stock does not behave like this, check which rifle in the family you are actually holding.
steps.aside: FN's removal instruction: Push the buttstock module downward and off the receiver assembly backplate (Figure 35).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §16.1 heading, p.31

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide rod out of the rear
steps.action: With the backplate clear, pull the recoil spring and guide rod assembly straight out of the rear of the receiver.
steps.prose: On a .308 this is a stouter spring than the 16S's and it has been holding the carrier forward, so there is a short resistance at the start and then nothing. It comes out as one assembly. Keep it off a gritty bench — it runs the full length of the receiver and anything it collects ends up under the bolt carrier on reassembly.
steps.quote: Remove recoil spring / guide rod assembly by pulling it out of the rear of the receiver (Figure 36).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.3 Removal of the moving parts assembly, step 3, p.38

steps.title: Bolt carrier out, charging handle left forward
steps.action: Leave the charging handle fully forward, reach inside the rear of the receiver and slide the bolt carrier assembly out. Then separate the bolt carrier body from the bolt carrier front rail.
steps.prose: The handle must stay forward or it fouls the carrier on the way out — that is why FN writes it into the instruction. There is an easier route on a heavy 17S carrier: hold the handle forward and locked, put your hand at the rear of the receiver, raise the muzzle, and let the carrier body and front rail slide out into your palm. Have that hand in place first, because a .308 bolt carrier landing on a concrete floor is not a small event.
steps.quote: While leaving the charging handle fully forward, reach inside of the receiver and slide the bolt carrier assembly out of the rear of the receiver (Figure 37). Separate the bolt carrier body from the bolt carrier front rail (Figure 38)
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.3 Removal of the moving parts assembly, step 4, p.38

steps.title: Both charging handles out at the rearmost opening
steps.action: Draw the charging handles rearward until they align with the rearmost opening in their slots, then pull both of them straight out.
steps.prose: Two handles, one each side, each leaving only where its slot widens right at the back. Lined up, they lift out with no effort; a fraction off and neither will move, which is a positioning problem rather than a stuck part. This step is the clearest confirmation you are on the right book: a first-generation 17S has one handle and it reciprocates.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handles rearward until they align with the rear most opening in the charging handle slots. Remove both charging handles by pulling them out (Figure 39).
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.3 Removal of the moving parts assembly, step 5, p.38

steps.title: Charging sled out — and stop there
steps.action: Reach inside the receiver and slide the charging sled out of the rear. Do not take the sled apart any further.
steps.prose: The sled is what the two handles drive, and it is the last piece out of the receiver. It looks as though it should come apart and it must not — the same notice that governs this whole strip warns that attempting to disassemble the inner mechanism assemblies can damage the rifle beyond repair or lose small parts. Out, cleaned, back in.
steps.quote: Reaching inside the receiver, slide the charging sled out of the rear of the receiver (Figure 40). Do not disassemble the charging sled beyond this point.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.3 Removal of the moving parts assembly, step 6, p.38

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Receiver and .308 barrel, trigger module, carbine buttstock module, recoil spring and guide rod, bolt carrier body and front rail, two charging handles, charging sled, magazine — all with finger pressure and no tools.
steps.prose: That reaches the bore and chamber from the breech end, the receiver interior, the carrier and its rail, the sled, and the outside of the trigger module. FN's schedule is a clean after every day of shooting and sooner if the session got dirty, with a minimum clean being a wipe-down plus lubrication of key parts. Splitting the bolt out of the carrier, and pulling the gas regulator and piston, are published here and sit behind Deep Clean.
steps.quote: NOTICE! THE FOLLOWING DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURES ARE DESIGNED TO BE PERFORMED WITH FINGER PRESSURE ONLY AND NO TOOLS ARE REQUIRED.
steps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19 Disassembly, notice, p.36

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out right to left, then the bolt
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin out of the carrier body from right to left, using the corner of one of the charging handles or a punch. Take the firing pin out of the rear, the bolt cam pin out of the left side of the bolt, then pull the bolt out of the front of the carrier body.
deepSteps.prose: Right to left is FN's stated direction, and the corner of a charging handle being an acceptable tool tells you how much force belongs here. Once the retaining pin is out the firing pin is loose, so keep the carrier nose-down over the bench. Stop at the bolt: FN says not to disassemble the bolt assembly and not to take the buffer off the carrier body — on a .308 that buffer is doing real work and it is not a user item.
deepSteps.aside: FN's limit: Remove the bolt from the front of the bolt carrier body (Figure 44). Do not disassemble the bolt assembly. Do not disassemble the buffer from the bolt carrier body.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin from the rear of the bolt carrier body (Figure 42).
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.4 Disassembly of the moving parts assembly, step 6, p.40

deepSteps.title: Gas regulator out, then the piston driven out with its tool
deepSteps.action: With the trigger module, buttstock and moving parts already out, take the heat shield out if one is fitted, set the regulator to 2 o'clock, then push the detent in with a small flathead and turn the regulator clockwise to 3 o'clock. Take it out towards the front of the gas block and out through the receiver opening. Muzzle down on a soft surface, thread the piston removal tool onto an 8-32 cleaning rod, run it in from the rear along the upper interior rails until it touches the rear of the piston, and tap softly until the tool body meets the gas block; the piston then comes out the front of the gas block through the receiver window.
deepSteps.prose: This is the only tooled part of the SCAR strip and both tools are specific — a small flathead for the detent and FN's own piston removal tool on a threaded rod. Softly is the word that matters on the tapping: the tool bottoming on the gas block is the stop, not the point at which to hit harder. Take the heat shield out first if one is installed; FN says it makes the regulator and piston easier to reach, and on a 17S it genuinely does.
deepSteps.quote: Use a small flathead screwdriver or similar tool to push in on the gas regulator detent and turn the gas regulator clockwise to the 3 o’clock position (Figure 45 A-B).
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §19.5 Removal of the gas regulator and gas piston, step 8, p.41

deepSteps.title: Gas system dry: piston wiped, ports picked, nothing oiled
deepSteps.action: Wipe the gas piston with a cloth, using a bronze bristle brush where carbon has built up. Check the gas ports in the regulator and clear them with a dental pick if they are fouled. Put no lubricant on the piston, the regulator or the gas block.
deepSteps.prose: This is the SCAR's defining bench rule and it is the opposite of what habit suggests: the gas system runs dry, and lubricant in there bakes to a varnish that seizes the regulator and can damage the rifle. Carbon on the piston is normal; blocked regulator ports are not, and on a .308 running a heavier gas impulse they are what turns a smooth rifle into one that beats itself. The vent hole in the front of the regulator is the designed escape route for that carbon, so keep it clear.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the gas ports in the gas regulator to ensure they are free of debris and carbon build-up.
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §20.1 Cleaning procedures, step 9, p.44
deepSteps.warn: NOTICE! DO NOT APPLY LUBRICANT TO THE GAS PISTON, GAS REGULATOR OR GAS BLOCK, THESE COMPONENTS ARE NOT TO BE LUBRICATED IN ANY WAY. USING LUBRICATION IN THE GAS SYSTEM COULD DAMAGE YOUR RIFLE.

deepSteps.title: Trigger module: lower the hammer under your thumb
deepSteps.action: With the module out of the receiver, move the safety selector to off safe, put your thumb over the hammer and pull the trigger, keeping tension and lowering the hammer slowly to its forward rest. Clean the group with a polymer-safe aerosol cleaner, let it dry, and lightly lubricate the trigger and hammer contact points.
deepSteps.prose: Out of the rifle there is no bolt carrier to catch the hammer, so a released hammer runs into its own stop at full speed — which is the damage FN warns about. Thumb on it, trigger pulled, lowered under control. Clean it where it sits: the instruction is not to alter or attempt to disassemble any part of the module, and any service on it goes to the FN Service Center or your armorer.
deepSteps.quote: Release the hammer by placing your thumb over the hammer and pulling the trigger. Be sure to keep tension on the hammer and lower it slowly to the forward resting position.
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §20.2 Cleaning the trigger module, step 4, p.45
deepSteps.warn: NOTICE! NEVER ALLOW THE HAMMER TO SLAM FORWARD, THIS MAY DAMAGE THE TRIGGER MODULE.

deepSteps.title: Bore: bronze all the way through, stainless never
deepSteps.action: Clean the .308 bore from the breech with a rod, brass jag and a snug patch wet with military-grade cleaner. For heavy fouling use a bronze bore brush, pushed completely through before it is withdrawn. Use an M16-style chamber brush sized for the chamber, rotated clockwise several times, then wipe dry and pass one lightly lubricated patch for preservation.
deepSteps.prose: A stainless brush cuts the chrome lining out of the barrel and there is no recovering that. Pushing the bronze brush all the way through before reversing is what keeps bristles out of the rifling. Keep the rod off the crown — FN singles it out because damage there costs accuracy directly, and on a .308 that people shoot at distance the crown is the last thing the bullet touches.
deepSteps.quote: NOTICE! DO NOT USE A STAINLESS-STEEL BRUSH TO CLEAN THE BORE. IT COULD DAMAGE THE CHROME PLATING.
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §20.1 Cleaning procedures, step 3, p.44

deepSteps.title: Suppressed 17S: the 10 o'clock setting and the warranty line
deepSteps.action: If this 17S is shot suppressed, use a properly installed forward-venting suppressor and move the gas regulator to the 10 o'clock suppressed position. Watch for a rifle running too fast — heavier recoil, more gas at the ejection port, cases thrown further and further forward than unsuppressed.
deepSteps.prose: FN puts this in warranty language, which is the plainest signal it gives about back pressure: a correctly installed forward-venting can such as the QD762 does not affect the rifle's warranty, while damage from improperly installed devices or high-back-pressure cans is not covered. The book is careful to say the 10 o'clock setting does not guarantee safe and reliable operation with all suppressors. Aftermarket muzzle devices must be fitted by a qualified gunsmith with bore concentricity checked before use.
deepSteps.aside: FN's suppressed setting: 10 o'clock setting - Suppressed operation. Does not guarantee safe and reliable operation with all suppressors (Figure 16).
deepSteps.quote: A properly installed forward-venting suppressor, such as the FN QD556 and QD762, on your SCAR rifle will not affect the warranty of your rifle.
deepSteps.cite: FN SCAR® 16S, 17S AND 20S SECOND GENERATION AUTOLOADING RIFLE OWNER'S MANUAL — 2512-SCAR 16S/17S/20S-OM 38-101764 — §14.1 Firing procedures, suppressor note, p.27

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER & LOCKING LUGS
tasks: Rod with a brass jag and a snug patch wet with military-grade cleaner, from the breech end, worked back and forth several times
Keep the rod off the muzzle crown — damage there directly affects accuracy on a .308
Heavy fouling: bronze bore brush pushed completely through before withdrawing, so bristles do not break off in the rifling
Never a stainless steel brush; it damages the chrome plating
M16-style chamber brush sized for the chamber, cleaner applied, rotated clockwise several times
Wipe chamber and bore dry, then a lightly lubricated patch for preservation, and check no patch has been left inside

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, BOLT GROUP & SLED
tasks: Small brush or rag through the receiver interior and the rest of the action, then light lubricant on the moving parts
Small brush and cleaner on the bolt, carrier body, carrier rail and charging sled; wipe dry and reassemble
Wipe all exposed metal with a lightly oiled cloth, taking finger marks off — they are where moisture collects
Give the metal a light film of oil any time the rifle has seen weather or handling

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM, TRIGGER & MAGAZINE
tasks: Cloth on the gas piston, bronze bristle brush for baked carbon
Dental pick through the regulator's gas ports if they are fouled
No lubricant of any kind on the piston, regulator or gas block
Trigger module: polymer-safe aerosol cleaner, dried, then very light lubricant on trigger and hammer contact points only
Magazine: polymer-safe aerosol cleaner inside and out, drained, dried with compressed air or air-dried and lightly oiled — FN does not recommend disassembling it
Keep 17S and 20S magazines together and 16S magazines separate; they share a well pattern with the 20S and not with the 16S

reassembly: Gas piston into the gas block with the gas rings towards the muzzle and their notches NOT aligned, then the regulator in with the detent pressed and rotated counterclockwise to 2 o'clock.

Bolt into the front of the carrier body with the extractor on the right, cam pin in with its tab horizontal, firing pin in from the rear, retaining pin seated firmly — it will not finish flush with the carrier.
Charging sled into the rear of the receiver, then both charging handles refitted at the rearmost slot openings.
Bolt carrier assembly back in from the rear, then the recoil spring and guide rod assembly.
Carbine buttstock module up onto the backplate, then the trigger module rotated into place and the takedown pin pressed home from the right.
Safety selector confirmed on safe, external surfaces wiped down, then the function check.
fncheck: With the 17S empty and reassembled, FN's check is short and exact: operate the charging handle and confirm the bolt assembly moves freely; operate the safety selector and confirm it moves between on safe and off safe freely; leave the selector on safe. Add two of your own — the gas regulator should click through 2, 10 and 3 o'clock on its detent without sticking and be left at 2 o'clock, and an empty 20-round magazine should seat and drop free, which is also the check that you have not picked up a 16S magazine by mistake.
